deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 62-66 of the dossier). Grothendieck is studying a finite arrangement Σ of pseudo-lines in a topological projective plane X. He also studies an auxiliary space 𝒳: a modular or configuration space of a 'moving' pseudo-line D relative to Σ, stratified by the cells of the arrangement. On the previous page he computed the monodromy u_D : π1(𝒳, F_D) → Aut(F_D). He found it surjective, and that the only nontrivial character is χ_×. The character χ_c is trivial by a parity argument: the weight of a path from D to D' is congruent mod 2 to sing_{D'} − sing_D, where sing_D is the number of vertices of Σ lying on D.

This page (dated 3.1.84) is a local gluing analysis attached to an elementary specialization D → D'.
- D' is the special pseudo-line, passing through a vertex s of Σ where two pseudo-lines of Σ cross (orange curves). D is a nearby generic one.
- To each pseudo-line he attaches a disc: Δ_D and Δ_{D'}. These are presumably the 2-cells or 'rideaux' over Pol(D), whose boundaries carry the cyclic structure of the arrangement read along D.
- On ∂Δ_{D'} there are two distinguished antipodal 'transition arcs' a, a' (near s and its antipode).
- On ∂Δ_D there are two privileged arcs: b (the transition arc, where the crossing at s is resolved) and b' (its antipode).

Gluing count. A 'standard' gluing of Δ_D to Δ_{D'} identifies one arc α ∈ {a, a'} with one arc β ∈ {b, b'}, with one of two orientations σ. This gives 2·2·2 = 8 a priori ways to build a surface with boundary whose associated graph is Γ_Σ = Γ.

Reduction. The antipodal involutions act on both discs. The choice (α, β, σ) and its antipodal transform (α', β', σ') give isomorphic surfaces. These correspond to the two 'circularisations' (cyclic orientations) of Γ and the corresponding privileged transition arcs for the associated local orientations. So up to isomorphism there are 4 cases. By composing with antipodisms one may normalize β = b, so that the vertex s appears next to the chosen transition arc on the glued surface. He remarks this 'looks a bit idiotic' when s lies opposite.

What follows (next page). He asks which choice admits a natural map from the glued surface to X, canonical on each disc. The naive answer forces α = a; shrinking the discs to Δ* with boundary through s also allows α = a'. He argues the natural choice is α = a', the 'rive' that 'faces' the specialization, rather than the parallel-transported one. With that choice the map from the glued surface (𝔛) to X is an immersion.

Purpose. This is a step toward a cellular or 2-dimensional model of the space of pseudo-lines relative to Σ (its local gluing across a wall/vertex stratum) and its natural immersion into the plane. It complements the π1/monodromy computation of the previous page.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The count 8 = 2×2×2 and the quotient by the antipodal symmetry (8 → 4) are consistent.

The machine reading 'il n'y a pas que deux cas différents' is inconsistent with the argument. Since antipodal pairs are identified, 8 choices give 4 surfaces, and the next lines speak of 'les quatre choix (en fait, les huit)'.
The claim that antipodal pairs give isomorphic surfaces is asserted with only a brief justification (correspondence with the two circularisations of Γ). It is plausible but not proved on the page.

ideas.what: Enumerating the gluings of the discs attached to a generic pseudo-line D and its specialization D' (through a vertex s) along transition/antipodal boundary arcs: 8 a priori, 4 up to the antipodal involution.
ideas.modern_name: Local cell structure / wall-crossing in the space of one-element extensions of a rank-3 oriented matroid (space of pseudolines relative to an arrangement)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Extension spaces: Sturmfels–Ziegler (1993); Mnëv–Richter-Gebert; Goodman–Pollack for pseudoline spaces

ideas.what: Using antipodal maps on both discs and the two cyclic orientations ('circularisations') of the graph Γ_Σ to identify gluings pairwise.
ideas.modern_name: Quotient by the antipodal/orientation-reversal symmetry (two reorientations of a cyclic arrangement graph)

ideas.what: Choosing the gluing so that the glued surface maps naturally into the plane X as an immersion (developed on the next page).
ideas.modern_name: Developing map / immersion of a cell complex of pseudolines into the projective plane

missed.claim: Together with the neighbouring pages, Grothendieck builds a cellular/surface model of the space of pseudo-lines relative to a fixed arrangement Σ. He computes its π1 monodromy and characters, and studies gluing across vertex strata. This is the extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid, studied later and independently (Sturmfels–Ziegler 1993, Mnëv–Richter-Gebert). Grothendieck's monodromy/character viewpoint (χ_×, χ_S, χ_c on π1) on this space is not part of that literature.
missed.quote: huit façons "standard" de recoller Δ_D à Δ_{D'} ... de construire une surface à bord avec le graphe Γ_Σ = Γ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an early, independent treatment of the topology of pseudoline extension spaces, a topic central to the extension space conjecture, with a fundamental-group/monodromy angle. It could be of historical interest. Its mathematical novelty on this page specifically is low.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine local combinatorial bookkeeping step: counting the 8 gluings and reducing them to 4 by antipodal symmetry. It belongs to a larger, little-known Grothendieck project on pseudo-line spaces that anticipates oriented-matroid extension-space topology. That project context is mildly interesting, but this page alone contains no striking result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: read 'huit façons "standard" de recoller Δ_D à Δ_{D'}, suivant les bords' rather than 'des recollement ... suivant [-les-]'.
Read 'il n'y a que quatre cas différents de surfaces' (not 'pas que deux'), consistent with 8/2 = 4 and 'les quatre choix (en fait, les huit)'.
'car la surface obtenue par un choix (α, β, σ) de recollement et (α', β', σ')' rather than 'sa [?] ... ou des recolle'.
'ils correspondent aux deux circularisations de Γ, et les arcs privilégiés de transition pour les or. loc. correspondantes': 'inflexibles' is likely 'privilégiés'.
Last lines: 'Pour les quatre choix (en fait, les huit) qui' rather than 'Pourquoi'.
'D'où huit façons a priori de construire une surface à bord (éventuellement)': 'a priori' and 'éventuellement' are insertions above the line.
